description: A `type` alias covers only its type expression; the words after it are a second token run on the line after a complete statement, so the alias owes a `;`: E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON after `number` and after `not` (§7.2.2 rule 7), never silently dropped.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S478 "⭐ RULED — open owner questions, PA recs adopted wholesale" item 2 (g-boot-body-top-trailing-tokens-vs-semicolon-s478) — re-pinned from E-UNQUOTED-DISPLAY-TEXT ×2
rationale: §7.2.2 (S469) governs, superseding §40.8's S441 round-5 line reading ("The tokens after the end, on the statement's own line, are `E-UNQUOTED-DISPLAY-TEXT`"): a line break is whitespace (rule 4), and a second token run after a complete statement is E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON after the first (rule 7). The bytes are still covered by an error, so §40.8's coverage invariant holds. The follow-on parse errors on `extra` / `more words` are a separate cascade, not asserted. (S479 s479-parse-fails — two edits so the case grades the `;` rule alone: (1) the second alias was `"a" | "b"`, a string-literal union, which is not a SPEC type form (§7.5 `type-expr ::= primitive-type | identifier | type-expr '[]' | type-expr '|' type-expr | type-expr '?' | fn-type` — no literal member); it is re-spelled `number | not`, a union both front ends read (a general union such as `number | string` is refused by name in the bootstrap, whose type system has `T | not` only). (2) The line after the aliases was `console.log("after")` with no `;`, a THIRD E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON under §7.2.2 rule 1 ("every statement that is not block-like … SHALL end with `;`"; the body top is rules 1–9), which the ruled count of 2 does not include; it is now `@count = 2;`, a terminated body-top statement both front ends compile, still showing that the statement after the aliases is read, not swallowed.)
